# Active Workflows

The active workflows separate product checks, release publication and research:

- `ci.yml`: unconditional lint/tests/branch coverage plus the repository-required build status. The `build` job depends on an always-running `production-local` Linux/macOS/Windows matrix that executes the Workbench plus Phase 4 and Phase 5 production-local acceptance tests. `build` runs with `always()` and explicitly fails unless the matrix result is `success`, so a production-local matrix failure or cancellation cannot be hidden behind a skipped required status. This is the safe always-reporting enforcement path for production acceptance; it does not rely on a path-filtered workflow being configured as an unconditional required check.
- `workbench-ci.yml`: focused Workbench tests, clean wheel-extra installation, CLI checks, and headless UI smoke tests. Runs on relevant pull requests and explicit dispatch. This checks legacy Gradio compatibility; it does not establish that its optional dependency closure is secure.
- `workbench-portability.yml`: clean-install portability checks on Linux, macOS, and Windows, the Phase 4 and Phase 5 production-local adversarial suites, plus the legacy Workbench container build. Runs on relevant pull requests and explicit dispatch. The unconditional `ci.yml` production-local matrix remains the repository-layer production gate.
- `research-package-ci.yml`: research-package boundary and import checks. Runs on relevant pull requests targeting `main` and explicit dispatch.
- `standalone-workbench.yml`: the legacy product quality gate and Gradio-containing frozen builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Runs on relevant pull requests and explicit dispatch. These artifacts are not used for the web-only 0.12.4 release and do not inherit its dependency-audit result.
- `web-client-ci.yml`: static client build, packaged asset verification and API contracts. Runs on relevant pull requests, relevant pushes to `main`, and explicit dispatch.
- `web-only-distribution-candidate.yml`: strict audit of the actual web shipping dependency closure, followed by Linux/macOS/Windows frozen builds and HTTP chat smoke tests. Runs on every pull-request head without path filters, so engine, client, helper and validation changes cannot silently reuse older package evidence. Supports explicit dispatch for the release workflow. Artifacts remain unapproved candidates.
- `release-workbench.yml`: explicitly triggered, fail-closed prerelease publication for the current protected `main` SHA. A maintainer selects `RELEASE`. Preflight requires successful exact-SHA main-push `ci.yml`, then dispatches fresh exact-SHA Workbench, portability, research, web-client and web-only distribution runs. Only the web-only artifacts are collected. It rechecks archive hashes against their candidate manifests, requires one Linux, Windows and macOS bundle, validates frozen/HTTP/roundtrip evidence, and promotes manifests to `approval_scope: research-preview`. It verifies the SBOM, provenance, wheel/sdist installation, and complete checksum inventory. Before publication, the pinned `actions/attest` action attests every subject and the checksum manifest. The workflow rechecks `main` and verifies the downloadable release. Production-local promotion additionally follows `docs/operations/production-local-release.md`; publication alone does not establish the final production claim.
- `production-release-assurance.yml`: binds to an exact published tag, is dispatched automatically after publication (or manually), and is verification-only. It has read-only release/attestation permissions, no OIDC token authority, and no attestation-write capability. It first verifies that the published `SHA256SUMS` was attested by the trusted `release-workbench.yml` signer, requires the checksum manifest to cover exactly the published file set, checksum-verifies all bytes, validates provenance/manifests, and verifies every subject against the trusted Release Workbench signer. This is the final cryptographic verification gate for the production-local candidate; the signing authority remains in the pre-publication Release Workbench workflow. Native Apple notarization and Windows Authenticode are not claimed.
- `open-set-hf-review.yml`: manually triggered Hugging Face open-set research runs.
- `slm-model-benefit.yml`: manually triggered small-language-model benefit runs.
- `qwen7b-capability-scaling-once.yml`: research-only capability reference, triggered by changes to that workflow in a pull request targeting `main`.

Original retired workflows remain under `archive/source-workflows/` for provenance only.
